headline: Highest risk is medium prompt-injection and cascading-error exposure from Khoj’s shared indexed notes into an undocumented LlamaFactory interaction; no direct data-leak or compliance pathway is evidenced.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Khoj reads indexed personal notes/files and supports shared index across user clients, so attacker-controlled content in those notes could influence downstream interpretation. LlamaFactory has no documented ingestion path, but because the pairwise interaction is undocumented and uncertainty must escalate, I rate this medium rather than low. No direct shared channel is shown, so higher severities are not justified.
conditions: IF Khoj indexes attacker-controlled notes that LlamaFactory later consumes as training or prompt data, injection becomes plausible.
IF a shared workspace or export/import step is added between the agents, the pathway strengthens.
mitigations: Restrict Khoj to trusted note sources only.
Add a manual review step before any Khoj output is reused by LlamaFactory.
Keep the agents on separate workspaces.
requires-engineering: add provenance tagging for imported text.
requires-engineering: sanitize or strip instruction-like content before reuse.

B_data_leakage.rationale: Khoj touches personal notes and indexed documents, but LlamaFactory has no filesystem read, no network egress, and no data classes touched. There is no shared workspace, OAuth principal, or documented transfer path, so a leakage route between the pair is not evidenced. The absence of B-side ingress makes this provably blocked from the provided profiles.
conditions: IF LlamaFactory gains filesystem read or an import pipeline from Khoj, leakage becomes possible.
IF both agents are later placed under a shared authenticated workspace, reassess.
mitigations: Keep LlamaFactory isolated from Khoj storage.
Do not export personal notes into LlamaFactory.
Verify no shared cloud sync or mounted volume exists.
requires-engineering: enforce per-agent storage separation.
requires-engineering: add access logging for any future import path.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Khoj can read files and use broad network egress, while LlamaFactory has neither filesystem read nor network egress and no write capabilities. With no overlapping write surface, git state, or shared mutable resource, there is no capability conflict pathway in the supplied profiles. The pair is asymmetric rather than conflicting.
conditions: IF LlamaFactory is later granted write access to the same directory Khoj reads, conflict risk appears.
IF either agent is connected to a shared mutable database or git repo, reassess.
mitigations: Keep write permissions disabled for both agents.
Avoid mounting a shared mutable directory.
Separate any future databases by agent.
requires-engineering: add locking if shared state is introduced.
requires-engineering: define ownership boundaries for any shared resource.

D_cascading_error.rationale: Khoj can surface retrieved notes and documents, and LlamaFactory is a fine-tuning/instruction-tuning system that could treat imported text as training or prompt material. If Khoj output is reused without verification, errors or hallucinations can cascade into model artifacts. The interaction is undocumented, so uncertainty pushes this to medium rather than low.
conditions: IF Khoj output is fed into LlamaFactory training or evaluation without human review, cascading error is plausible.
IF LlamaFactory is used to generate support content from Khoj retrievals, downstream mistakes can propagate.
mitigations: Require human review of Khoj outputs before reuse.
Use a small validation set to spot-check imported text.
Label retrieved content as untrusted in prompts.
requires-engineering: add verification gates before training ingestion.
requires-engineering: track source provenance through the pipeline.

E_compliance.rationale: Khoj touches personal notes and indexed documents, which may carry regulated data, while LlamaFactory is unverified and shows no data handling or residency claims. There is no documented cross-border or retention mismatch, so only a low compliance concern is supported. The lack of B-side compliance metadata limits the finding and prevents escalation.
conditions: IF regulated personal data is stored in Khoj and exported into LlamaFactory workflows, compliance review is required.
IF LlamaFactory is deployed in a jurisdiction with stricter residency or retention rules, reassess.
mitigations: Avoid placing regulated data in Khoj exports.
Document retention for any shared artifacts.
Review whether any export crosses jurisdictional boundaries.
requires-engineering: add data-class filtering before export.
requires-engineering: publish retention and deletion policies for both systems.
